coverageNote: Topic-level, paraphrased, non-authoritative. This file maps the AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (with revised points of focus, 2022) so a SOC 2 Type II effort can be tracked criterion-by-criterion. What is and is not solid here, stated plainly: (1) The criterion IDENTIFIERS are the strongest part, and every one of the 61 entries carries one in relatedControlCode with a codeVerifiedBy citation. They were not researched -- they were read directly out of the AICPA criteria document itself, which is freely published (a free account is required, so a reader cannot verify them merely by clicking the citation). The enumeration was extracted twice, from two independently obtained copies of that document -- the second downloaded from the AICPA page cited here -- and the two agreed exactly, 61 of 61, series by series. Verified enumeration: 33 common criteria (CC1.1-CC1.5, CC2.1-CC2.3, CC3.1-CC3.4, CC4.1-CC4.2, CC5.1-CC5.3, CC6.1-CC6.8, CC7.1-CC7.5, CC8.1, CC9.1-CC9.2), plus A1.1-A1.3, C1.1-C1.2, PI1.1-PI1.5, plus 18 privacy criteria (P1.1, P2.1, P3.1-P3.2, P4.1-P4.3, P5.1-P5.2, P6.1-P6.7, P7.1, P8.1). Two checks are worth recording because skipping either would have produced confident wrong output: the document's P<n>.0 tokens are section headers rather than criteria, confirmed by reading what follows each; and the first extraction regex was anchored to the expected answer and could not have matched a CC10 or a P9, so it was re-run unanchored -- CC10, CC0, CC8.2, CC9.3, A1.4, PI1.6, PI2, P0, P2.2, P6.8 and P8.2 are all absent. (2) Each entry's topicSummary is a PARAPHRASE describing what the criterion covers and what satisfying it looks like operationally. It is not AICPA's criterion text and not its points of focus, both of which are copyrighted and deliberately absent from this repo, exactly as HITRUST's MyCSF requirement wording is. Every summary was mechanically checked against the full text of the canonical AICPA download, and none shares a run of 8 or more consecutive words with it; the four that did on the first such check were rewritten. Treat a topicSummary as a prompt for the right conversation, never as the criterion itself. (3) Privacy previously shipped at series granularity (8 entries) because public secondary sources disagreed about its breakdown -- one enumerated 15 criteria with P6 ending at P6.2, another said roughly 18, a third conflated the 8 series with 8 criteria. All three were wrong or imprecise; P6 in fact runs P6.1-P6.7. That disagreement was resolved by reading the primary document rather than by searching harder, which is the general lesson: a canonical identifier is read, never researched. (4) Only the Security/common criteria are mandatory. Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity and Privacy are opt-in and, until an engagement selects them, belong at not_applicable -- see the skill's scope flow, which records that selection before the interview starts. Consult the AICPA Trust Services Criteria document or your CPA firm for exact criterion text, points of focus, and scope before relying on this for a real audit.

controls.topicLabel: Commitment to integrity and ethical values
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 1. Does the company actually run on the ethics it states? What gets tested is a code of conduct staff have signed, plus evidence that breaching it had a consequence at least once.
evidenceExamples: Signed code-of-conduct acknowledgements for all staff
Record of a conduct violation and how it was handled

controls.topicLabel: Board independence and oversight of internal control
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 2. Someone above management is genuinely watching security -- a board or equivalent body whose members do not report to the people they oversee, with minutes showing security was really discussed.
evidenceExamples: Board or security-committee meeting minutes covering security matters
Documented board composition showing independence

controls.topicLabel: Organizational structure, reporting lines, authority and responsibility
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 3. Security has named owners, a place in the reporting chain, and stated decision rights. An org chart plus written role definitions is what evidences it.
evidenceExamples: Current org chart
Written security role definitions and named owners

controls.topicLabel: Attracting, developing and retaining competent individuals
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 4. Hiring, screening and continued training produce people capable of running the controls -- background checks at hire, tracked security training thereafter.
evidenceExamples: Background-check records for new hires
Security awareness training completion report
Job descriptions listing required competencies

controls.topicLabel: Accountability for internal control responsibilities
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 5. Security duties carry consequences: they show up in performance reviews, and falling short is actually actionable rather than nominally so.
evidenceExamples: Performance review template including security responsibilities
Evidence of sanctions applied for a policy violation

controls.topicLabel: Relevant, quality information to support internal control
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 13. Control performance has to be observable. Logs, asset inventories and metrics are what let management see whether controls work, instead of assuming they do.
evidenceExamples: Asset inventory
Security metrics or dashboard reviewed by management

controls.topicLabel: Internal communication of objectives and responsibilities
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 14. Staff know which policies bind them, what their security duties are, and how to raise a concern -- evidenced by distribution and acknowledgement records, not by a policy merely existing.
evidenceExamples: Policy distribution and acknowledgement records
Internal security channel or all-hands security update
Documented whistleblower / security reporting path

controls.topicLabel: External communication on matters affecting internal control
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 15. The organization communicates with external parties about matters affecting the functioning of internal control -- customer commitments, breach notification paths, and how outsiders can report a vulnerability.
evidenceExamples: Public security page or trust center
Customer-facing SLA / security commitments
Vulnerability disclosure contact and process

controls.topicLabel: Specifying objectives clearly enough to assess risk against them
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 6. Objectives are stated precisely enough that a risk against them can actually be named and rated. Vague objectives make every downstream risk score unfalsifiable.
evidenceExamples: Documented security objectives tied to service commitments

controls.topicLabel: Identifying and analyzing risk to objectives
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 7. A real, current, documented risk assessment -- threats named, analyzed, and each given an owner and a treatment decision, rather than a spreadsheet refreshed the week before fieldwork.
evidenceExamples: Completed risk assessment / risk register with owners and treatment
Evidence the assessment was refreshed within the observation period

controls.topicLabel: Considering the potential for fraud
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 8. Fraud is treated as its own risk category, including insiders abusing privileged access -- not folded into 'external attacker' and then forgotten.
evidenceExamples: Fraud risk explicitly addressed in the risk register

controls.topicLabel: Identifying and assessing changes that could affect internal control
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 9. Big changes get re-assessed for their effect on the control environment: a new product, a new cloud region, an acquisition, or a shift in what regulators demand.
evidenceExamples: Risk reassessment triggered by a significant change during the period

controls.topicLabel: Ongoing and separate evaluations of control effectiveness
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 16. Someone checks the controls independently of whoever operates them -- internal audit, control self-assessment or continuous monitoring -- and does it during the period, not only before fieldwork.
evidenceExamples: Internal control review or internal audit report
Continuous-monitoring tool findings over the period

controls.topicLabel: Evaluating and communicating control deficiencies
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 17. Findings reach the people who can fix them, carrying an owner and a date, and escalate upward when severity warrants.
evidenceExamples: Deficiency log with remediation owners and dates
Evidence findings were escalated to management

controls.topicLabel: Selecting and developing control activities that mitigate risk
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 10. Every control traces back to a risk identified under CC3. A control matrix with no link to the risk register is a checklist, not a control environment.
evidenceExamples: Control matrix mapping each control to the risk it treats

controls.topicLabel: General control activities over technology
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 11. The IT general controls layer -- access, change and operations -- that everything at the application level quietly rests on.
evidenceExamples: Documented IT general controls (access, change, operations)

controls.topicLabel: Deploying controls through policies and procedures
controls.topicSummary: COSO Principle 12. Policy states what is expected and procedure states how; for a Type II there also has to be evidence that people followed the procedure all period.
evidenceExamples: Annual policy review and approval records
Procedure runbooks referenced by operators

controls.topicLabel: Logical access security over protected information assets
controls.topicSummary: The identity and encryption backbone: single sign-on, MFA, network segmentation, and encryption of data both in transit and at rest.
evidenceExamples: MFA enforcement configuration for all production access
TLS 1.2+ enforced on external endpoints
Encryption-at-rest settings for databases and object storage

controls.topicLabel: User registration, authorization and credential removal
controls.topicSummary: The joiner-and-leaver control. Credentials are issued only after approval and revoked when someone departs; how fast deprovisioning happens is among the most heavily sampled items in a Type II.
evidenceExamples: Access request/approval tickets for new joiners
Termination checklist showing access revoked, with timestamps

controls.topicLabel: Role-based access, least privilege and segregation of duties
controls.topicSummary: Who can reach what, by role, at least privilege, with incompatible duties kept apart. Periodic access reviews are how this gets shown across a period rather than at a single moment.
evidenceExamples: Quarterly user access review with reviewer sign-off and resulting revocations
Role-to-permission matrix

controls.topicLabel: Physical access restriction to facilities and assets
controls.topicSummary: Physical access to facilities and equipment. For a cloud-hosted service most of this is inherited from the hosting provider -- name that inheritance rather than claiming a control you do not operate.
evidenceExamples: Office badge access logs and review
Cloud provider's own SOC 2 report covering data center physical security

controls.topicLabel: Secure disposal of physical assets holding data
controls.topicSummary: Before hardware leaves your hands, whatever was on it has to be genuinely unrecoverable -- secure wipe, cryptographic erase or certified destruction, with a record kept.
evidenceExamples: Certificates of destruction for decommissioned media
Device wipe records for returned laptops

controls.topicLabel: Protection against threats from outside the system boundary
controls.topicSummary: Defenses at the boundary: firewalls and security groups, WAF and DDoS protection, hardened remote administration, and keeping internal services off the public internet.
evidenceExamples: Firewall / security group rule set and its review
VPN or zero-trust access configuration for remote administration

controls.topicLabel: Restricting transmission, movement and removal of information
controls.topicSummary: Controlling how information travels -- encrypted on the wire, restricted onto removable media, and watched by data-loss tooling where the risk justifies it.
evidenceExamples: Removable media restriction enforced via MDM
DLP rule configuration
Enforced encryption on data transfers to third parties

controls.topicLabel: Preventing or detecting unauthorized or malicious software
controls.topicSummary: Stopping or catching software nobody approved: endpoint protection, application allowlisting, and integrity monitoring on production hosts.
evidenceExamples: EDR / anti-malware deployment coverage report
File integrity monitoring alerts and their disposition

controls.topicLabel: Detecting configuration changes and new vulnerabilities
controls.topicSummary: Knowing when the estate drifts or a fresh weakness lands -- vulnerability scanning on a stated cadence, plus alerting when a hardened baseline changes underneath you.
evidenceExamples: Vulnerability scan reports across the observation period
Remediation SLA tracking by severity
Hardening baseline and drift alerts

controls.topicLabel: Monitoring components for anomalies indicating malicious acts
controls.topicSummary: Centralized logging that something or someone actually watches. Retaining logs nobody reads does not satisfy this.
evidenceExamples: SIEM / centralized log pipeline configuration
Alert rules and a sample of alerts triaged during the period

controls.topicLabel: Evaluating security events to determine whether they are incidents
controls.topicSummary: The triage step between an alert and a declared incident: a stated severity scale, and a record of how events were judged against it.
evidenceExamples: Incident severity classification criteria
Triage records for events evaluated during the period

controls.topicLabel: Responding to identified security incidents
controls.topicSummary: A response plan with named roles, contact paths and decision rights -- who declares an incident, who tells customers, who tells regulators.
evidenceExamples: Incident response plan with named roles and contacts
Post-incident reviews for incidents during the period
Tabletop exercise record

controls.topicLabel: Recovering from identified security incidents
controls.topicSummary: Getting back to normal after an incident, and proving the cause was truly dealt with rather than the symptom having merely stopped.
requiredPolicies: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
evidenceExamples: Recovery steps documented in post-incident reviews
Root-cause corrective actions tracked to closure

controls.topicLabel: Authorizing, testing, approving and implementing changes
controls.topicSummary: The entire change-management program hangs off this single criterion: changes are authorized, built, tested, reviewed and approved before they reach production. Every change made during the period is a sampling population.
evidenceExamples: Pull requests showing peer review and approval before merge
CI pipeline enforcing tests before deploy
Separation of development, staging and production environments
Emergency change records with retrospective approval

controls.topicLabel: Risk mitigation activities for business disruptions
controls.topicSummary: Planning for the disruption you have not had yet -- impact analysis, continuity plans that actually get exercised, and insurance for whatever risk is left over.
requiredPolicies: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
evidenceExamples: Business impact analysis
Business continuity plan and evidence it was exercised
Cyber insurance policy

controls.topicLabel: Vendor and business partner risk management
controls.topicSummary: Vendor risk end to end: diligence before signing, security terms in the contract, and continued review -- including reading your subservice organizations' own SOC 2 reports and the CUECs they push back onto you.
evidenceExamples: Vendor inventory with risk tiering
Security reviews for critical vendors during the period
Collected subservice organization SOC 2 reports and CUEC review

controls.topicLabel: Capacity management
controls.topicSummary: Watching headroom before it runs out -- utilization monitoring, thresholds that trigger action, and a way to add capacity in time to matter.
evidenceExamples: Capacity monitoring dashboards and thresholds
Autoscaling configuration
Capacity review records

controls.topicLabel: Environmental protections, backup and recovery infrastructure
controls.topicSummary: The machinery availability actually rests on: redundancy, failover, backups that run and are monitored, and the physical and environmental protections underneath -- much of it inherited from a cloud provider.
requiredPolicies: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
evidenceExamples: Backup schedule and success/failure monitoring
Redundancy and failover architecture
Cloud provider environmental controls inherited via their SOC 2

controls.topicLabel: Testing recovery plan procedures
controls.topicSummary: A backup nobody has ever restored is not evidence. This is the restore test, with recovery objectives measured rather than asserted.
requiredPolicies: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
evidenceExamples: Backup restoration test results within the observation period
Disaster recovery exercise report with RTO/RPO measured

controls.topicLabel: Identifying and maintaining confidential information
controls.topicSummary: The organization identifies and maintains confidential information to meet its objectives related to confidentiality -- you cannot protect a category of data you have not defined, inventoried, and labelled.
evidenceExamples: Data classification scheme
Inventory of systems holding confidential data
Labelling or tagging in practice

controls.topicLabel: Disposing of confidential information
controls.topicSummary: The organization disposes of confidential information to meet its objectives related to confidentiality -- retention periods that are defined, enforced, and actually result in deletion.
evidenceExamples: Retention schedule by data type
Evidence of automated deletion jobs running
Customer data deletion on contract termination

controls.topicLabel: Information about system processing objectives and specifications
controls.topicSummary: Publishing what the system is meant to do with data, precisely enough that 'processed correctly' has a definition to be measured against.
evidenceExamples: Published API and data specifications
Documented definitions of processed data

controls.topicLabel: Controls over system inputs
controls.topicSummary: What arrives gets checked before it is trusted -- is the batch whole, are the values plausible, and what happens to a record that fails.
evidenceExamples: Input validation rules and rejection handling
Reconciliation of received record counts

controls.topicLabel: Controls over system processing
controls.topicSummary: Processing itself is controlled, with failures surfaced and exceptions worked rather than silently dropped on the floor.
evidenceExamples: Job failure alerting and exception queues
Evidence of exceptions investigated and resolved

controls.topicLabel: Controls over system outputs
controls.topicSummary: What leaves is whole, correct and on time, reconciled back against what went in.
evidenceExamples: Output reconciliation controls
Delivery SLA monitoring

controls.topicLabel: Controls over storage of inputs, items in processing and outputs
controls.topicSummary: Inputs, work in progress and outputs are all stored intact, and kept for as long as the specification calls for.
evidenceExamples: Storage integrity checks
Retention of processing records per specification

controls.domain: Privacy: Notice and Communication of Objectives
controls.topicLabel: Notice to data subjects of privacy practices
controls.topicSummary: Data subjects are given notice of the organization's privacy practices -- what personal information is collected, for what purposes, and how it is used, retained, disclosed and disposed of. The notice has to reach them when it is actually relevant, not merely exist somewhere on the site.
evidenceExamples: Published privacy notice and its version history
Evidence the notice is surfaced at the point of collection

controls.topicLabel: Communicating choices and obtaining consent
controls.topicSummary: The choices a data subject has over collection, use, retention, disclosure and disposal of their personal information are communicated to them, and consent is obtained wherever the organization's privacy objectives require it.
evidenceExamples: Consent capture records
Opt-out mechanism and evidence it is honored

controls.topicLabel: Collection consistent with stated objectives
controls.topicSummary: Personal information is collected only in ways consistent with the organization's stated privacy objectives -- purpose limitation applied at the point of collection, rather than reconciled afterwards.
evidenceExamples: Data inventory mapping each collected field to a stated purpose

controls.topicLabel: Explicit consent where required
controls.topicSummary: Where a category of personal information requires explicit consent, the organization communicates what it is seeking consent for and records that consent before collecting.
evidenceExamples: Explicit-consent records for sensitive data categories

controls.topicLabel: Use limited to the purposes in the notice
controls.topicSummary: Use of personal information is limited to the purposes identified in the privacy notice and covered by consent. A new purpose needs new notice or new consent -- not a reinterpretation of the old one.
evidenceExamples: Records showing secondary uses were assessed against the notice

controls.topicLabel: Retention consistent with objectives
controls.topicSummary: Personal information is retained only as long as the organization's privacy objectives require, against a defined retention schedule rather than indefinitely by default.
evidenceExamples: Retention schedule covering personal information
Evidence retention limits are enforced, not just documented

controls.topicLabel: Secure disposal
controls.topicSummary: Personal information is securely disposed of once its retention period ends, such that it cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
evidenceExamples: Automated deletion job records
Deletion on customer contract termination

controls.topicLabel: Data subject access to their own information
controls.topicSummary: Data subjects who have been identified and authenticated can access the personal information the organization holds about them.
evidenceExamples: Data subject access request log with response times
Identity verification step in the request flow

controls.topicLabel: Correction, amendment and appending
controls.topicSummary: The organization corrects, amends or appends personal information on a data subject's request, and communicates the outcome -- including when it declines and why.
evidenceExamples: Correction request records showing outcomes communicated

controls.topicLabel: Disclosure to third parties with consent
controls.topicSummary: Sharing outside the company is confined to the purposes the notice already told people about, with consent wherever your privacy objectives call for it.
evidenceExamples: Third-party disclosure register with the purpose and consent basis for each

controls.topicLabel: Record of authorized disclosures
controls.topicSummary: Every disclosure you were permitted to make still has to be written down -- who received it, when, and under which purpose. That register is what makes the accounting in P6.7 possible at all.
evidenceExamples: Authorized disclosure log

controls.topicLabel: Record of unauthorized disclosures and breaches
controls.topicSummary: The same discipline applies to disclosures that were never authorized: a complete, accurate and timely record of unauthorized disclosures detected or reported, including breaches.
evidenceExamples: Unauthorized disclosure and breach register

controls.topicLabel: Privacy commitments obtained from third parties
controls.topicSummary: Anyone outside the company who can touch this data owes you binding privacy commitments matching your own, flowed down in the contract rather than assumed from a vendor's marketing page.
evidenceExamples: Data processing agreements or privacy terms for vendors handling personal information

controls.topicLabel: Third-party commitment to notify of unauthorized disclosure
controls.topicSummary: Those same third parties also commit to telling the organization about actual or suspected unauthorized disclosure. Without that commitment the organization's own notification deadlines under P6.6 are not achievable.
evidenceExamples: Contractual breach-notification clauses and their agreed timelines

controls.topicLabel: Notification of breaches and incidents
controls.topicSummary: The organization notifies affected data subjects, regulators and other required parties of breaches and incidents involving personal information, within whatever deadlines apply to it.
evidenceExamples: Breach notification procedure with statutory deadlines
Notifications actually issued during the period, with dates

controls.topicLabel: Accounting of personal information held and disclosed
controls.topicSummary: On request, the organization provides a data subject with an accounting of the personal information it holds about them and of whom it has been shared with.
evidenceExamples: Sample accounting produced in response to a data subject request

controls.topicLabel: Accuracy, currency, completeness and relevance
controls.topicSummary: Personal information is kept accurate, current, complete and relevant for the purposes it was collected for. Stale personal data is a privacy defect here, not merely a data-quality one.
evidenceExamples: Data quality checks over personal information
Correction workflow feeding back into source systems

controls.topicLabel: Handling privacy inquiries, complaints and disputes
controls.topicSummary: Someone owns privacy complaints end to end: a route in, a named owner, a resolution, and a reply telling the person what actually happened.
evidenceExamples: Privacy complaint log with resolutions and timelines
Periodic review of privacy compliance
